invariants.name: normalized-hypothesis-priors
invariants.expected: priors are finite, within [0,1], unique by ID and sum to 1

invariants.name: complete-action-utility-matrix
invariants.expected: each action has a finite utility for every hypothesis

invariants.name: bounded-observation-likelihoods
invariants.expected: each survey supplies one finite positive-outcome likelihood per hypothesis in [0,1]

invariants.name: effort-budget-respected
invariants.expected: selected portfolio effort does not exceed the declared budget

invariants.name: decision-value-objective
invariants.expected: selection maximizes net EVSI and includes the no-observation option

invariants.name: stable-permutation-invariance
invariants.expected: reordering candidate survey inputs does not change the canonical plan or scores

negativeControls.mutation: Change one prior so the prior probabilities no longer sum to one.
negativeControls.reason: Posterior and expected-utility calculations require a normalized prior.

negativeControls.mutation: Set one outcome likelihood below zero or above one.
negativeControls.reason: A likelihood must be a valid probability.

negativeControls.mutation: Remove one hypothesis utility from an action.
negativeControls.reason: The action utility matrix must cover the hypothesis space.

negativeControls.mutation: Reorder candidate surveys without changing their content.
negativeControls.reason: Plan selection must not depend on transport ordering.

negativeControls.mutation: Make all actions utility-equivalent across hypotheses while keeping informative surveys.
negativeControls.reason: Information without a possible decision improvement has zero gross EVSI and should not be purchased at positive cost.

qualification.referenceOracle: Exact enumeration is the correctness oracle for small synthetic cases.
qualification.productionTarget: Compare against human survey selection, fixed priority, EIG ranking, random selection and a clairvoyant upper bound under matched budgets.
qualification.statisticalGate: Likelihood calibration and utility sensitivity must be reported separately; synthetic values do not qualify a real-world planner.
